labs.title: Configure Data Lake Storage for analytics in the Azure portal
labs.summary: Create an Azure Storage account with hierarchical namespace, prepare raw and curated containers, upload sample data, grant least-privilege ACLs, and add a lifecycle rule.
labs.scenario: Contoso is centralizing monthly sales extracts for analytics. In the **simulated Azure portal** on your lab VM, create a storage account named **stcontosodatalake01** in **rg-data-platform** with **Hierarchical namespace** enabled for Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2. Keep blob anonymous access disabled. Create private containers **raw** and **curated**, upload the provided VM files into **raw/sales/2026/09**, grant the **Analysts** group **Read + Execute** on the curated directory, and add a lifecycle management rule that moves raw blobs to Cool after 30 days.
learningObjectives: Create a storage account for analytics with a hierarchical namespace
Organize structured, semi-structured, and unstructured files in containers and directories
Apply ACL and lifecycle settings that match an analytics data lake scenario
prerequisites: Know what Azure Storage accounts, containers, and blobs are

steps.title: Open the storage account create experience
steps.instruction: In the portal menu, select **Storage accounts**, then select **+ Create**.
steps.hint: The command bar is under the Storage accounts page title.
steps.explanation: Storage accounts are the Azure resource that host containers and blobs. Data Lake Storage Gen2 capabilities are enabled on the storage account.

rules.description: You opened the Create a storage account page

steps.title: Create a Data Lake Storage Gen2 account
steps.instruction: Create **stcontosodatalake01** in **rg-data-platform** and **(Europe) West Europe**. On **Advanced**, turn on **Enable hierarchical namespace** and keep **Allow enabling anonymous access on individual containers** off. Then select **Create**.
steps.hint: Hierarchical namespace is on the Advanced tab. It is the setting that changes the account from a flat blob namespace to Data Lake Storage Gen2 semantics.
steps.explanation: A hierarchical namespace enables directory operations and POSIX-like ACLs, which are important for analytics data lakes.

rules.description: Storage account stcontosodatalake01 exists in rg-data-platform
rules.failureFeedback: Create stcontosodatalake01 in rg-data-platform and West Europe.

rules.description: Hierarchical namespace is enabled and anonymous access is disabled
rules.failureFeedback: Turn on hierarchical namespace and keep anonymous access disabled.

steps.title: Create private raw and curated containers
steps.instruction: Open the storage account, select **Containers**, and create **raw** and **curated** with **Private (no anonymous access)**.
steps.hint: Create one container at a time with the New container form.
steps.explanation: Raw is a landing zone for source files; curated is for cleaned data that analysts can consume.

rules.failureFeedback: Create raw as a private container.
Create curated as a private container.

steps.title: Upload the September files to raw
steps.instruction: In **Storage browser**, create **sales/2026/09** in **raw** and upload **sales-2026-09.csv**, **customers.json**, and **product-photos.zip** from the VM. Classify them as structured CSV, semi-structured JSON, and unstructured binary, and choose **Parquet** as the optimized analytics format.
steps.hint: CSV and JSON are common exchange formats. Parquet is columnar, so analytics engines can scan fewer bytes when queries use a subset of columns.
steps.explanation: The raw zone preserves source files; later ETL or ELT jobs can convert frequently queried data to Parquet tables.

rules.failureFeedback: Create sales/2026/09 in the raw container.

rules.description: All three files are uploaded with correct classifications
rules.failureFeedback: Upload and classify the CSV, JSON, and ZIP files correctly.

steps.title: Grant least-privilege ACLs on curated
steps.instruction: Open **curated | Manage ACL** and grant **Analysts** **Read** and **Execute** only. Do not grant **Write**.
steps.hint: Execute is required to traverse a directory; Write would allow the group to change curated data.
steps.explanation: Data lake ACLs let you combine broad Azure roles with fine-grained directory permissions.

rules.description: Analysts have Read + Execute but not Write on curated
rules.failureFeedback: Grant Analysts Read and Execute only on curated.

steps.title: Add a lifecycle management rule
steps.instruction: Select **Lifecycle management** and add **move-raw-to-cool**. Use **Limit blobs with filters**, prefix **raw/sales/**, and move matching blobs to **Cool** after **30** days. You may leave the optional Archive action at **180** days.
steps.hint: Lifecycle rules use prefixes to target selected blobs such as one landing folder.
steps.explanation: Lifecycle management automates movement between access tiers as data ages.

rules.description: Lifecycle rule moves raw sales blobs to Cool after 30 days
rules.failureFeedback: Add move-raw-to-cool with prefix raw/sales/ and Cool after 30 days.

labs.solution:
1. Select **Storage accounts** and **+ Create**.
2. **Basics**: Resource group **rg-data-platform**, name `stcontosodatalake01`, Region **(Europe) West Europe**, Performance **Standard**, Redundancy **Locally-redundant storage (LRS)**.
3. **Advanced**: turn on **Enable hierarchical namespace** and keep **Allow enabling anonymous access on individual containers** off. **Create**, then **Go to resource**.
4. Open **Containers**. Create `raw` and `curated`, both with **Private (no anonymous access)**.
5. Open **Storage browser**. In `raw`, create `sales/2026/09` and upload `sales-2026-09.csv`, `customers.json`, and `product-photos.zip`; classify them as structured CSV, semi-structured JSON, and unstructured binary. Choose **Parquet** as the optimized analytics format.
6. Open **curated | Manage ACL**. Add **Analysts** with **Read** and **Execute** only.
7. Open **Lifecycle management**. Add `move-raw-to-cool`, scope **Limit blobs with filters**, prefix `raw/sales/`, move to Cool after `30` days, optional Archive after `180` days.
